versions: Edge pickup geometry simplified. Team describes improved shooting through successive Israeli events; intermediate dimensions not fully enumerated.

context_documents.title: 2022-1577 · Broad pickup and controlled low-spin release require local jam relief
context_documents.body:
# 2022-1577: Broad pickup and controlled low-spin release require local jam relief

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A broad flat-belt/polycord collector feeds color-based rear rejection and a conveyor. Early edge-vectoring features were removed after simultaneous-ball jams. Adjustable hood arcs and powered back contacts manage release spin; climb sequencing uses contact/current cues.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The retained source ties collector simplification to two-ball reliability rather than minimum part count for its own sake.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A wide acquisition face can deliver multiple pieces into a narrower region, so pair tests are more informative than isolated pickup speed. Current-based climb transition detection needs a threshold robust to friction and battery state.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test adjacent cargo, wrong-color ordering and climb sensor false positives; do not assume lower spin is always optimal without trajectory data.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/WrTNg9g2tJ4](https://youtu.be/WrTNg9g2tJ4)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with Steampunk at Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:37–3:34 dribbler; 3:44–5:48 diversion and shooter; 6:00–7:50 sensing and shot; 8:28–11:20 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: Flat belt and polycord dribbler lost its beveled edges after paired cargo wedged.
A reversible wheel directs cargo toward either rear ejection or the elevator, with separate infrared confirmations.
Fixed and moving hood arcs interleave. Static hooks and telescopes alternate support.
source_reviews.limitations: Automatic captions blur some names. The interview establishes contact order and team intent, with no measured layouts or event-by-event shot results.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Oasis combined a broad ground mouth with an early routing decision. The robot did not need to take an unwanted ball all the way to its launcher to clear it. The price of that separation was an extra exit and a decision point that still needed positive contact while the wheel changed direction. The top launcher had its own mechanical adjustment so launch elevation could be varied independently of the incoming path.
piece_flow: Flat belt and polycord contacts deliver cargo to the back of the intake.
At the sorter, an intake roller and powered directional wheel contact the ball. Color is checked against alliance assignment.
Rejected cargo contacts an upper wheel and exits rearward. Accepted cargo moves against the interior guide and up the conveyor, with infrared confirmation.
The conveyor presents cargo to the main wheel, back wheels and adjustable hood.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The feed branch sits low enough to sort before lifting. Its rear discharge needs an uninterrupted volume through the chassis and a clear exit in the robot’s driving and climb poses. The launcher requires an interleaving swept volume for the hood, while the spring-and-winch climber needs room to tilt the telescopes around the static supports.

subsystems.name: Wide dribbler
subsystems.construction: Flat belt and polycord make a broad contacting surface. Early bevels at the sides were removed.
subsystems.operation: Present multiple approach angles to the mouth and carry a ball back to the sorter.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted a large contacting area and found pairs could enter and become stuck with the bevel geometry.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Acquisition width and useful throughput are different quantities. A narrowing path can convert a successful two-ball pickup into a persistent bridge.
subsystems.interfaces: Both edges ultimately feed a common decision region.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test two nearly touching balls at the center and both edges. Inspect belt tracking and a worn cord’s effect on the crossing.
subsystems.unknowns: Pulley sizes, tension, entrance gap and permissible speed are unresolved.

subsystems.name: Early color diversion
subsystems.construction: Reversible omni-directional contact, intake back roller, an additional upper wheel on the rear path, and infrared confirmation on the paths.
subsystems.operation: Choose inward travel for alliance cargo or outward travel for rejection, then repeat for the next piece.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team describes automatic sorting from the field alliance assignment.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Early rejection saves downstream travel only if the preceding intake can hold the next ball while the sorter clears. The exit sensor can distinguish a completed rejection from a command that never moved cargo.
subsystems.interfaces: A classification dwell and exit confirmation couple the intake and conveyor.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test an incorrect color followed tightly by a correct one, then reverse the ordering. Cover one sensor to determine whether clearing is possible.
subsystems.unknowns: Unknown routing latency, sensor fault handling and eject velocity.

subsystems.name: Interleaving hood launcher
subsystems.construction: Machined fixed arcs mesh with moving arcs. Main and back wheels control release and spin.
subsystems.operation: Set angle and speed from target range, deliver cargo and tune the landing point inside the hub.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted reduced spin and reported aiming toward the interior back area to limit bounce-outs.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Arc overlap can maintain support over a broad elevation range. Its actual value depends on maintaining smooth entry and compression at both extremes.
subsystems.interfaces: Conveyor release and hood entrance need a shared geometry over the full adjustment.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check contact marks and shot dispersion with worn cargo, including the transition between fixed and moving segments.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured spin rate or shot table.

subsystems.name: Traversal climber
subsystems.construction: Telescopes, static hooks with contact switches, springs, rope winch and a tilt stop.
subsystems.operation: Pull onto a bar, settle onto static hooks, tilt and extend toward the next rung, then use motor resistance as an engagement cue.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team describes automated advances and reports about ten seconds to traversal.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Motor load can also indicate binding, so verify capture with an independent state before releasing support.
subsystems.interfaces: Static hooks and telescope tips must land at compatible robot pitch.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test one-sided contact and sensor disagreement before permitting load transfer.
subsystems.unknowns: Unknown hook geometry and timed success distribution.

revisions: Removed edge bevels after jams. Shooter tuning evolved, but hardware changes between Israeli events remain unresolved.
transferable_principles: Route rejected pieces before consuming the long feed path when an independently clear exit is available.
Tune for scored arrivals, including post-impact behavior inside the goal.
disconfirming_conditions: In a game without wrong-color pieces, diversion adds a failure point unless it serves another required exit.
A narrower collector can win if the bottleneck remains the sorter.
remaining_gaps: Exact competition configuration by event, classification latency and field climb reliability.
recommended_images: Request side views of accepted and rejected paths through the sorter and a close view of the hood at both limits.
